title: Profiling Urban Streets: A Semi-Supervised Prediction Model Based on Street View Imagery and Spatial Topology

problem.claim: The study aims to predict functional and socioeconomic indicators for street segments represented by multiple street view images.

gap.claim: Existing modeling must address the spatial distribution of multiple images on a street and the spatial topology of streets.

contributions.claim: The authors present a semi-supervised Urban Street Profiling Model based on street view imagery and spatial adjacency of urban streets.

The model combines spatial context-based contrastive image learning, LSTM-based multi-image fusion, SPHINX-generated street-scene descriptions, and semi-supervised graph learning over an adjacency-based urban street graph.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report conducting experiments with real-world datasets to assess USPM.
The authors report that USPM considerably outperforms baseline methods in two urban prediction tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Urban profiling using multimodal datasets is motivated by city expansion and growth.
Street view imagery is useful for understanding urban characteristics because of its visual information and correlations with human activities.
Street-segment prediction from multiple images requires modeling image spatial distributions and street adjacency.
USPM builds visual and textual street representations and further encodes them with semi-supervised graph learning over spatial topology.
Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to show improved performance over baselines on two urban prediction tasks.

unknowns: The specific functional and socioeconomic indicators and prediction tasks are not identified.
Dataset sizes, geographic coverage, label proportions, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
No ablation results or details about the semi-supervised learning setup are provided.
